instruction: Judge whether the AI output is correct. Accept correct output and reject incorrect output. Do not assume every output contains an error.

items.prompt: Return the length of the longest consecutive run in a list.
items.ai_output: for i in range(1, len(values) - 1): inspect(values[i])
items.ground_truth: The final index is not inspected; the exclusive stop must be len(values).
items.verification_basis: Trace [7, 7] and a run ending at the final item.

items.prompt: Return the last valid index of a non-empty array.
items.ground_truth: Array indices are zero-based, so the final valid index is length minus one.
items.verification_basis: Check arrays of length one and length three.

items.prompt: A single pass over n values keeps two counters and performs constant-time work per value.
items.ai_output: The algorithm is O(n log n) because it updates the maximum inside the loop.
items.ground_truth: The maximum update is constant time; one pass is O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
items.verification_basis: Count loop iterations and distinguish constant work from logarithmic work.

items.prompt: A balanced binary search halves the remaining candidate interval each iteration.
items.ai_output: The search takes O(log n) time and O(1) auxiliary space when implemented iteratively.
items.ground_truth: The stated bounds match the iterative balanced-search assumptions.
items.verification_basis: State the sorted-input and balanced-partition assumptions.

items.prompt: Two workers increment the same shared counter.
items.ai_output: The increment is safe because reading and writing an integer are each atomic.
items.ground_truth: Read-modify-write is not one atomic operation; increments can be lost without synchronization or an atomic increment.
items.verification_basis: Interleave two reads before either write and observe the lost update.

items.prompt: Parse a transaction amount from an external record.
items.ai_output: Call toInt() and let malformed or missing values fail; upstream data should already be valid.
items.ground_truth: The boundary must define missing, malformed, range, and currency behavior rather than assuming upstream validity.
items.verification_basis: Test missing, malformed, negative, overflow, and unsupported-currency inputs.

items.prompt: Parse a JSON response using Python requests.
items.ground_truth: The requests library exposes response.json(); requests.get_json(response) is not the documented API.
items.verification_basis: Check the official library API documentation and a minimal isolated call.

items.prompt: How should a service use a cloud credential in production?
items.ai_output: Inject a short-lived, least-privilege credential at runtime, keep it out of source and logs, and rotate it when exposure is suspected.
items.ground_truth: The output states the expected secret-management controls.
items.verification_basis: Check source, artifact, log, scope, lifetime, and rotation controls.

items.prompt: Debit a ledger and write its audit event.
items.ai_output: Write the ledger first and the audit row second; if the audit write fails, retry only that row.
items.ground_truth: Independent writes can expose an unaudited debit; use one transaction where possible or an explicit outbox/idempotent reconciliation design.
items.verification_basis: Inject failure between writes and inspect the observable state and recovery path.

items.prompt: A stream consumer checkpoints after processing a payment event.
items.ai_output: The checkpoint guarantees the payment will never be applied twice.
items.ground_truth: A crash between the business write and checkpoint can cause replay; downstream effects must be idempotent.
items.verification_basis: Crash at each boundary and replay the same event ID.

items.prompt: Explain why a test can pass while the implementation is still wrong.
items.ai_output: A test only establishes the cases and oracle it exercises. If the cases omit a boundary or the oracle encodes the same assumption as the implementation, the test can pass while the broader contract is false.
items.ground_truth: The explanation correctly distinguishes tested evidence from the full behavioral contract.
items.verification_basis: Construct a shared-fault oracle and an untested boundary case.

items.prompt: Two workers update a shared counter.
items.ai_output: Use an atomic increment or a lock whose scope covers the read-modify-write operation.
items.ground_truth: The output names synchronization that protects the complete update operation.
items.verification_basis: Inspect the synchronization scope and run an interleaving stress test.

items.prompt: Parse a JSON response using Python requests.
items.ground_truth: The response object exposes the documented json() method.
items.verification_basis: Check the official API documentation and a minimal isolated call.

items.prompt: A parser accepts external transaction records.
items.ai_output: Reject malformed, missing, out-of-range, and unsupported-currency values with stable diagnostics; test each boundary explicitly.
items.ground_truth: The output defines defensive input handling and testable boundary behavior.
items.verification_basis: Review the validation contract and execute representative boundary cases.

scoring.accept_correct: 1 when a correct output is accepted
scoring.reject_incorrect: 1 when an incorrect output is rejected

verification_status: Ground truth is authored from explicit code, API, concurrency, security, and consistency invariants; independent review is required before participant exposure.
